decisions.reason: As a core airfield-lighting control product with visible post-launch support and strong fit to the firm's automation strategy, it is likely performing at or near aspiration and slack favors retention.

The surveillance display extends the firm's established integrated airport portfolio, and in a growing, R&D-active firm management would usually keep such a complementary system unless results were clearly below aspiration.

Training programs deepen customer relationships and support the installed base, so with moderate organizational slack the firm is likely to keep this offering even if its stand-alone results are still maturing.

This narrower training course shows the weakest market prominence and is the easiest to fold into broader training services, so if results lag aspiration management would likely reallocate those resources.

Collaboration software is closely aligned with the firm's stated move toward real-time information sharing and collaborative decision-making, making continued market presence more likely than withdrawal.

Although surveillance systems are resource-intensive and competitive, this product is strategically important and recent enough that a growing firm with R&D capability would usually allow more time before dropping it.
